title: Errors
notes: Random errors vary unpredictably between readings; repeated measurements and averaging reduce their influence. Systematic errors shift results consistently because of calibration, zero offset or method and are not removed by simple repetition.
Accuracy is closeness to an accepted value; precision is agreement among repeated readings. A set can be precise but inaccurate if a systematic offset is present.
If a true value is known, absolute error is |xmeasured−xtrue|; relative error is absolute error divided by the reference value; percentage error is 100 times relative error.
Example: readings 10.2, 10.3 and 10.1 cm average to 10.2 cm. Compared with accepted 10.0 cm, absolute error is 0.2 cm and percentage error is 2%.
Check an instrument’s zero before use, repeat readings where possible, report units and uncertainty, and avoid unsupported digits beyond the instrument resolution.
confusion: A small spread does not prove accuracy.
Do not report more digits than the instrument supports.
